narr: A late September moisture surge yielded isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms from roughly September 28 through the 30, some of which resulted in strong wind gusts. Some isolated flash flooding was noted in some southern Utah locations as well.
ev: Officials from Capitol Reef National Park reported 1 to 2 feet of water flowing through a wash that feeds into the Grand Wash, as well as 1 to 2 feet of water flowing through Grand Wash itself.

Zion National Park officials reported that normally dry washes near Canyon Junction were seeing flash flooding, that there were waterfalls on both sides of Zion Canyon, and that the campground had minor flooding. A thunderstorm which moved through produced an estimated 0.25 to 0.75 inches of rainfall per Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor 1-hour analysis.
lsr: 1-2 FEET OF WATER FLOWING THROUGH A WASH THAT FEEDS INTO THE GRAND WASH. THE GRAND WASH ITSELF HAD SEVERAL INCHES OF WATER.
